basic_identification.full_title: Trolley for Carrying Jute Bales — Specification (First Revision) (जूट के गट्ठो को ले जाने की ट्राली — विशिष्टि (पहला पुनरीक्षण))
basic_identification.sector_category: Mechanical Engineering / Non-powered Material Handling Equipment (approved by the Heavy Mechanical Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Non-powered Material Handling Equipment Sectional Committee, HMD 15, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Non-powered Material Handling Equipment Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This Indian Standard prescribes the principal dimensions, materials of construction, design configurations, load capacities, tolerances, and finishing requirements for hand-propelled trolleys designed specifically to transport dense jute bales up to a safe working capacity of 2 kN inside jute mills, excluding long-distance transport and public roads.

version_status_and_amendments.year_first_published: 1983 (originally adopted by the Indian Standards Institution in 1983, and revised to this active first revision in 1996)
version_status_and_amendments.amendment_slips: NIL (No amendments issued on this active reaffirmed copy)

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Mild steel tubes, tubulars and other wrought steel fittings: Part 1 Mild steel tubes (fifth revision)
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Provides dimensional, thickness, and tensile specifications for standard mild steel tubes used to fabricate the main trolley frame and handle.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Steel for general structural purposes (fourth revision)
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Provides metallurgical limits, yield strengths, and bending properties for steel sheets, round bars, and flats used in structural members, struts, and fouling guards.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Specification for wheels and castors (first revision)
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Regulates the manufacturing tolerances, load ratings, rubber-tyre qualities, and bearing configurations for the trolley's wheels.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Ready mixed paint, air drying, red oxide-zinc chrome, priming (second revision)
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Specifies weather-resistant, anti-corrosive priming paints applied to bare steel surfaces to protect the assembly against industrial humidity.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Enamel, synthetic, exterior: (a) undercoating, (b) finishing (second revision)
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Specifies glossy, impact-resistant synthetic enamel paint used to coat and seal the primed steel trolley frame.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Colours for ready mixed paints and enamels (third revision)
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Standardises the color shades and naming nomenclature for synthetic exterior enamel finishes.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Standardises the mathematical rounding of observed or calculated physical parameters, capacities, and dimensional clearances to determine code compliance.

allied_standards.title: Code of Practice on Occupational Safety and Health Audit
allied_standards.relevance: Directs safety audits in high-hazard textile and material handling yards. Hand-propelled trolleys must be audited for warp-free alignment and smooth rolling wheels to prevent worker strains and load-toppling accidents.

allied_standards.title: Occupational Health and Safety Management System
allied_standards.relevance: Unifies risk mitigation, requiring daily pre-shift physical audits of manual handling equipment, including tyres, wheel bearings, and load frames.

allied_standards.title: Code of Practice for General Steel Construction
allied_standards.relevance: The master structural steel code in India, regulating support steelwork, structural frames, and welding criteria. The structural welds on the MS tubes and flats of the trolley must satisfy IS 800 standards to prevent shear failure under maximum load.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification / Technical Construction Guidelines (Mechanical Engineering Department / Material Handling)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a BIS license to print or stamp the physical 'ISI Mark' on the manufacturer's nameplate or trolley frame. Compliance with IS 10506 is mandatory in public sector procurement tenders, textile corporation supply contracts, and industrial logistics audits across India.

requirements.detail: Any numerical value representing the result of a physical dimension, load capacity, or test analysis must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

The main load-bearing trolley frame must be fabricated out of mild steel tubes conforming to IS 1239 (Part 1) : 1990 or formed steel sections pressed from mild steel sheets conforming to IS 2062 : 1992.
The fully fabricated hand trolley must be rated and certified to safely receive, balance, and transport jute bales up to a maximum load carrying capacity of 2 kN (approx. 200 kg).

The wheel axle must be positioned precisely relative to the frame center of gravity to enable the operator to easily balance and push the trolley. The axle must be machined from solid round steel bar conforming to IS 2062 : 1992.
The steering handle must be constructed from robust mild steel tube conforming to IS 1239 (Part 1) : 1990 to provide rigid control during movement.

To prevent the loose fibers of the jute bales from touching, rubbing against, or wrapping around the rotating wheel assembly, the trolley must be equipped with fouling guards made from steel flats conforming to IS 2062 : 1992.

A support strut made of solid round steel bar conforming to IS 2062 : 1992 must be integrated into the frame. When the trolley is stationary, the structure must rest securely on its wheels and strut without tipping.
Although overall design dimensions are provided for reference, the permissible manufacturing tolerance on all overall dimensions of the trolley must not exceed ±5 mm.
The wheels must conform to IS 7369 : 1983, featuring solid rubber tyres and dust-sealed bearing arrangements to withstand the high-humidity, fiber-clogged floors of jute mills.
The finished trolley must undergo visual and mechanical alignment checks. The structural frame work must be completely free from warp, twist, or joint distortion.

The bare steel frame must be thoroughly cleaned of rust and grease with chemical solutions, given one coat of red oxide-zinc chrome priming paint conforming to IS 2074 : 1992, and finished with two coats of synthetic enamel paint conforming to IS 2932 : 1994 in an agreed shade conforming to IS 5 : 1978.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 10506 : 1996 (First Revision) is the primary national Indian Standard specification establishing technical, material, design, and performance requirements for non-powered hand trolleys used to carry dense jute bales inside textile mills. Maintained under the Non-powered Material Handling Equipment Sectional Committee (HMD 15) and reaffirmed in 2022, the code serves to standardise trolley manufacturing. It specifies a safe carrying capacity of 2 kN (approx. 200 kg), mandates robust materials such as IS 1239 steel tubes for the frame and IS 2062 steel flats for fouling guards and struts, limits manufacturing dimensional tolerances to a tight ±5 mm, requires standard rubber-tyred wheels conforming to IS 7369, and enforces a rigorous multi-coat red oxide synthetic enamel finish to protect the steel framework against rust and humidity in mill godowns.
